prompt.context: A widget manufacturer in Brazil has a 60% national market share and has a leadership position in South America. However, it only has a 5% international market share. The top 20 clients buy 80% of its products and the manufacturer is concerned with increasing margins and exploiting new sources of revenue.
prompt.question: Their CEO has asked you to gather data and brainstorm potential ideas for increasing margins and market share.

clarifying_info.q: How fast is the market growing?

clarifying_info.a: There are no significant competitors in the region. The greatest threat comes from U.S., Chinese, and Indian imports.

clarifying_info.q: How are products priced in the national market?
clarifying_info.a: The company uses premium pricing for national customers.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current capacity utilization of the plants?

clarifying_info.a: Plants cannot shift from producing one product to another.

clarifying_info.q: How does the company currently sell its products?
clarifying_info.a: The company currently sells products directly to customers.

clarifying_info.q: What products does the company sell and what are the unit economics?
clarifying_info.a: [Show Exhibit A] The company sells Products A, B, and C with different units, average prices, profit margin percentages, and unit costs.

clarifying_info.q: What is the breakdown of sales between national and international markets?
clarifying_info.a: [Show Exhibit B] Products are sold in both national and export markets at different prices and volumes.

exhibits.title: Product Overview
exhibits.shows: Table listing three products (A, B, C) with their total units, average price, profit margin percentage, and unit cost
exhibits.data: Product A: 400 units, avg price $9.00, 50% margin, unit cost $4.50; Product B: 200 units, avg price $5.50, 40% margin, unit cost $3.30; Product C: 100 units, avg price $4.00, 30% margin, unit cost $2.80

exhibits.title: National vs. Export Market Breakdown
exhibits.shows: Two tables showing national and export market data for each product: units sold and price per unit (profit margin fields are blank for the candidate to calculate)
exhibits.data: National — Product A: 200 units, $10 price; Product B: 150 units, $5 price; Product C: 75 units, $4 price. Export — Product A: 200 units, $8 price; Product B: 50 units, $6 price; Product C: 25 units, $4 price

framework: Understand market dynamics: size, growth rate, competitive landscape, and threat sources
Analyze product mix: profitability of each product (A, B, C) in national vs. international markets
Identify margin improvement levers: pricing, cost reduction, capacity expansion, product development
Identify market share growth levers: distribution channels, competitive response to imports, partnerships
Develop international expansion strategy: government support, acquisitions, new distribution channels
Recommend prioritized actions based on data analysis

questions.prompt: Calculate the profit margins for each product in the national and export markets (using unit costs from Exhibit A).
questions.guidance: Strong answer uses unit cost from Exhibit A and prices from Exhibit B to compute (Price - Unit Cost) / Price for each product-market combination, then compares margins across markets to identify which products are more profitable where.

math.setup: Profit Margin % = (Price - Unit Cost) / Price. Unit costs from Exhibit A: A=$4.50, B=$3.30, C=$2.80.
math.answer: National margins: A=55%, B=34%, C=30%. Export margins: A=44%, B=45%, C=30%. Product A is more profitable nationally; Product B is more profitable in export markets; Product C has equal margins in both markets.

questions.prompt: Based on the margin analysis, what strategic implications follow for the product and market mix?
questions.guidance: Should identify that Product A should be prioritized for national sales and Product B for international/export sales. Product C has identical margins in both markets. Plants cannot switch products, so capacity reallocation is limited — strategic response must focus on pricing, distribution, and partnerships rather than a simple production shift.

brainstorming.prompt: Brainstorm ideas for increasing margins and market share both nationally and internationally.

categories.name: National Market — Defend & Grow
ideas: Reduce prices selectively to compete with U.S., Chinese, and Indian imports and protect leadership position
Develop new products in partnership with local top clients (top 20 clients = 80% of revenue)
Establish new distribution channels to better serve smaller clients beyond the top 20
Invest in capacity expansion to accommodate demand growth (currently at 100% utilization)
Use premium pricing strategy to maintain margin advantage where competitive pressure is low

categories.name: International Market — Expand
ideas: Seek government support and commercial partnerships at the government level to aid export of products
Acquire a company in target international markets to gain distribution and customer base
Set up local distribution channels in priority export markets to reach customers directly
Focus international push on Product B given its higher export margin (45% vs. 34% nationally)
Explore joint ventures with regional distributors in target countries

categories.name: Operational / Cost Side
ideas: Review cost structure to identify cost reduction opportunities across all three products
Evaluate whether plants can be retrofitted or expanded to shift some capacity to higher-margin products
Negotiate better input costs given scale of operations

categories.name: Revenue Model
ideas: Explore bundling products A, B, C to increase wallet share with top clients
Develop service or maintenance contracts to create recurring revenue alongside product sales

recommendation: Nationally, prioritize Product A (55% margin) and consider selective price reductions to defend market share against U.S., Chinese, and Indian imports while maintaining premium positioning where imports are weak
Internationally, prioritize Product B (45% export margin) and seek government-level commercial partnerships to accelerate export growth; consider acquiring a local distributor in key target markets
risks: Capacity is fully utilized — any growth requires capital investment or productivity improvement
Price reductions to defend national share could erode margins if not carefully managed
International expansion is complex and slow; government partnership timelines are uncertain
Top 20 clients represent 80% of revenue — high concentration risk if any defect
next_steps: Quantify the investment required for capacity expansion and evaluate ROI
Identify and prioritize 2-3 target international markets with highest potential for Product B
Engage government trade bodies to explore export promotion programs
Develop a small-client distribution strategy to diversify the customer base beyond top 20
